extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, affected federal employees and their representatives (unions and employment lawyers), MSPB practitioners, and legal/policy stakeholders in federal civil service rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule preamble and response-to-comments clarifying OPM regulations (5 CFR part 302 and related parts) governing movement of positions/employees between the competitive and excepted services, employees' accrued procedural/appeal rights, and appeal routes to the MSPB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights are in addition to chapter 75/43 rights
rubrics_metrics.description: “The appeal rights conferred in this section are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any right the individual would otherwise have to appeal a subsequent personnel action undertaken without following appropriate procedures under chapter 75, subchapter II, or section 4303 of title 5, United States Code.” (Revised 5 CFR 302.603(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will revise 5 CFR 302.603(a) to state explicitly that the appeal right created by this rule provides an additional avenue for immediate correction and does not replace or waive other statutory appeal or procedural protections. This is intended to preserve any subsequently available chapter 75 or chapter 43 remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal when agency asserts move eliminates competitive status or protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the agency ... asserts that the move of the original position or any subsequent position ... will eliminate competitive status or any procedural and appeal rights that had previously accrued, the affected individual may appeal from that determination and request an order directing the agency (A) to correct the notice ... and (B) to comply with the requirements of either chapter 75, subchapter II or section 4303 of title 5, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised 5 CFR 302.602(b) allows affected individuals to seek correction of agency notices and orders requiring agencies to follow chapter 75/chapter 43 procedures where agency assertions would strip accrued rights, except where inconsistent with applicable statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal when agency fails to provide requisite notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the agency fails to comply with § 302.602(c)(1) of this part, and fails to provide an individual with the requisite notice, the affected individual may appeal and request an order directing the agency to comply with that provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will modify 302.603(c) to explicitly permit appeals based solely on a failure to give the notice required by the regulation (i.e., failure to inform individual of impacts on status/rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability for coerced or otherwise involuntary facially voluntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may appeal under this part on the basis that (A) a facially voluntary move was coerced or otherwise involuntary for purposes of this section or (B) a facially voluntary move to a new position would require the individual to relinquish their competitive status or any civil service protections and was coerced or was otherwise involuntary. (Added 5 CFR 302.603(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM adopts appeals for situations where an agency attempts to circumvent protections via 'voluntary' moves that were actually coerced or would force relinquishment of accrued rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule should not specify a separate time period for appeals; follow MSPB timing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM does not believe the final rule should specify a time period; the timing procedures should instead follow the normal processes associated with appeals to the MSPB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule will not add independent timing deadlines; appeals under the rule proceed under existing MSPB procedural timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM will not provide attorney-fee relief via regulation under 5 U.S.C. 7701
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will not adopt regulatory language bringing section 302.603 appeals under 5 U.S.C. 7701 to relieve successful appellants of attorney's fees or litigation costs because that goes beyond the scope of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters suggested this change, OPM declines to add it in the regulatory text and may consider options later if experience indicates change is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals under this part are treated like other MSPB appeals (procedural parity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeals described in 5 CFR 302.603 should be treated like all other appeals to the MSPB. Therefore, OPM does not believe that it should revise this final rule to account for the possibility of a lack of a MSPB quorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM explains MSPB procedures: Administrative judges (AJs) can issue initial decisions; if no petition for review, AJ decision becomes final; if petition filed, Board cannot issue decision until quorum restored; Clerk can grant withdrawal of a petition for review. Appeals under this rule follow these processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule does not cover SES positions (no SES inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM will not adopt the suggestion to clarify that the changes proposed within 5 CFR 302.603 include SES Positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM declines to extend the amendments to the Senior Executive Service for the same reasons it rejected similar suggestions elsewhere in the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of accrued property interest and chapter 75 protections
rubrics_metrics.description: By operation of law, certain Federal employees accrue a property interest in their continued employment and are entitled to adverse action rights under chapter 75 before they may be removed from career positions. Agencies are statutorily obligated to extend the specific protections codified at chapter 75 to eligible employees as defined in 5 U.S.C. 7511.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM interprets chapter 75 as precluding waiver of accrued statutory rights by the President, OPM, or an agency; this final rule clarifies and reinforces that point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making or policy-advocating character' should not expand exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The now-revoked Executive Order 13957 introduced a new conception of the phrase ... and sought to employ that conception to expand the category of employees excluded from adverse action procedural rights. This departed from established understanding (political appointees). OPM has determined that a regulation interpreting and clarifying this provision ... is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM intends the regulation to reaffirm the traditional understanding of that phrase (i.e., political appointees) and not to broaden exclusions from chapter 75 protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards and transparency measures for movements into the excepted service
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguards and measures may include agency reporting to OPM; OPM authorization to create certain new positions in—or move certain existing positions into—the excepted service; publication in the Federal Register; and an acknowledgment of the consent of affected employees when an existing employee obtains a different position in another service or schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These longstanding principles and safeguards are reinforced by the rule to ensure movements are an exception and are transparent and accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory necessity: not regulating is not viable due to fiscal and non-fiscal risks
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative to this rulemaking is to not issue a regulation. OPM has determined this is not a viable option. The risks of not issuing this final rule include fiscal costs (recruiting/replacing staff) and non-fiscal consequences (erosion of merit principles, loss of morale, service disruptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM's regulatory analysis finds promulgation prudent to preserve merit principles, settled expectations, and compliance with statutory enactments.

rubrics_metrics.name: This rule tracks the status quo and clarifies law; it is not intended to hamper legitimate performance management
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments to parts 210, 212, 432, and 752 clarify longstanding civil service law and agency procedures. Nor do commenters explain how the changes to part 302 ... would impact performance management. They are instead directed at potential movements of positions or employees ... and added for good administration, transparency, and to provide employees a right of appeal to the MSPB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM emphasizes the rule preserves existing performance management tools (chapters 43 and 75) and is not intended to make removal of legitimately poor performers more difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance management and misconduct are addressed under chapters 43 and 75; removal protections require congressional action to change
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal employee refuses to implement lawful direction from leadership, there are appropriate vehicles for agencies to respond through discipline and removal under chapter 75 or, alternatively, if performance related, chapter 43 and other authorities. ... OPM is not free to remove adverse action rights from large swathes of career civil servants. That is an action that may be taken only by congressional enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM rejects the argument that the rule unlawfully impedes performance management; it states statutory removal protections remain in place and can only be changed by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about use of FEVS survey data to justify prevalence of poor performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEVS data that commenters argued shows there are too many poor performers in government does not, in fact, show a numerical prevalence of poor performers. There is an important difference between (a) data showing a belief by respondents that poor performers exist and the agency has not adequately addressed their performance and (b) the existence of too many poor performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM explains limitations of survey evidence for policymaking: survey responses often reflect perceptions and lack supervisory detail; therefore they cannot alone show systemic prevalence of poor performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims of wholesale reclassification have alternative remedies beyond individual appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment expressed concern that individual appeals would be ineffective if an agency attempted to involuntarily move a majority of its workforce ('wholesale reclassification'). OPM noted there are ways to reschedule positions without infringing statutory protections and, to the extent 'wholesale reclassification' is unlawful, there exist other avenues to challenge such a move besides the processes in this final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM acknowledges limits of individual MSPB appeals in mass-movement scenarios and points stakeholders to other legal or administrative remedies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations of improper outside influence or ethics violations are outside scope of this rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether some civil servants are influenced improperly by outside corporations ... is outside the scope of this rule. But OPM notes that such demonstrable influence, to the extent it exists, could be a violation of federal ethics laws and ... could readily be addressed by existing performance management mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will not use this rule to address alleged corporate capture; such matters are addressed under ethics and performance regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM's authority: rules give effect to Congress' intentions under title 5 and are standard exercise of delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM is tasked by statute with the authority to execute, administer, and enforce all civil service rules and regulations as well as the laws governing the civil service. All of its rules give effect to Congress' intentions under title 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM frames the regulation as an appropriate exercise of its delegated authority to implement subchapter II of chapter 75 and to clarify protections for career employees.
